summary: Router 0.42.18 implements TM-03's next action 'Segment admin access' (ADR-0143, proposed). Traced B2: the control port app (app.build_apps) runs unexpected_error_middleware, then auth.basic_auth_middleware, for every route. The middleware passed /v1/ paths through before and still does (tunnel identity/approval, ADR-0136 enrollment networks, heartbeat token, one-time binary token). New: for every other path (UI and its files, /admin/*, /metrics) a non-empty router.admin_networks refuses a source address outside every network with 403 before the Basic Auth check, the ADR-0053 loopback switch and the failure counter. The address is request.remote, the TCP peer; aiohttp does not read X-Forwarded-For here, so a header cannot spoof it. values.in_networks maps IPv4-mapped IPv6 to IPv4 and puts non-addresses and None outside. Bypass via the /v1/ prefix was probed with a real aiohttp server (3.14.4): /v1/../admin/state, %2e%2e, %2F and mixed forms keep path.startswith('/v1/') true but resolve to 404, because aiohttp matches the literal path without dot-segment folding; the new test pins this against the real control app and pins the /v1/ routes to the three agent paths. The key is not in settings.EDITABLE; settings.coerce refuses it ('cannot be changed in the UI'), and Config.merged applies UI overrides only through roles, models, expose_concrete_models, clients and settings, so a stolen admin login cannot widen it. Config refuses non-CIDR lists and a list without loopback for a literal loopback control_listen (lockout). The agent calls only /v1/ on the control port (agent/*.go checked); deploy.py asks /admin/state over loopback on the router host, documented (include 127.0.0.1/32). Posture adds admin_from_any_network (info like control_on_network, so --init still writes no medium finding, ADR-0067; TM-03) for a network listener without the list. Default off, existing configurations unchanged. No new exception path.

tests.evidence: 10 tests. Rejected cases: outside addresses (plain, IPv4-mapped, other IPv6, None, non-address) get 403 on /, /ui.js, /ui.css, /favicon.ico, /admin/state, /admin/config, /metrics, /admin/ha and a PUT, also with valid credentials, reach no handler and leave _BASIC_SRC/_BASIC_FAIL/_BASIC_OK empty; the unauthenticated loopback switch does not open it; /v1/ dot-segment and encoded-slash paths resolve to 404 in the real control app, whose /v1/ routes are exactly the three agent paths; settings.apply refuses router.admin_networks; config refuses non-lists, invalid networks and a loopback listener without loopback. Accepted cases: no list = login decides as before; inside addresses (IPv4, mapped, IPv6) go on to the login; /v1/ paths pass; posture finding present/absent as intended. With auth.py, config.py and posture.py from origin/main: 47 failures, 1 error (the UI-settings case passes there too: it guards that the existing EDITABLE lock covers the new key).
unchanged expectations still hold (clean configuration is loopback, no new finding).

tests.command: every python test/... and tools/... command of all workflows in .github/workflows/, except run_tests.py and check_public_changes; plus ruff check ., router.py --check router/config.example.yaml --pure and node --check router/ui.js

tests.evidence: 337 PASS, 0 failures (the suite runs without router.admin_networks).

limitations: Behind a reverse proxy or a container runtime's userland proxy the router sees the proxy's address; segmentation then belongs to the proxy (documented).
Stolen admin credentials used from inside a listed network are not affected (out of scope for TM-03).
Not exercised against a live router with TLS in a browser; the middleware and the real control app's routing are tested in-process, the end-to-end suite runs without the key.
